thread:
lucas: quick roundup from the v3-compact bring-up — ran a mixed holdout (20k) with short/long query split and a couple of extra diagnostics.
priya: solid, what diagnostics did you add?
lucas: recall@1/5, median cosine-shift vs float32 baseline, silhouette for kmeans(200), and a KS test on norm distributions between quant variants.
ned: results please :)
lucas: top-line first:
- baseline float32 v2: r@1=0.81, r@5=0.93, median_cosine_shift=0.00 (baseline), silhouette_k200=0.42
- v3-compact int8-perchannel (pc): r@1=0.80, r@5=0.92, median_cosine_shift=0.015, silhouette_k200=0.40, norm_ks_p=0.12
- v3-compact int6-pertensor: r@1=0.74, r@5=0.89, median_cosine_shift=0.08, silhouette_k200=0.33, norm_ks_p=0.001
priya: int8-pc looks pretty close, int6 clearly degrades locality and cluster structure. KS p-value low for int6, so norm distribution changed significantly.
giulia: can you paste the eval command & seed so we can repro?
lucas: sure:
```
python eval/onboard_suite.py \
  --model v3-compact \
  --quant int8-perchannel \
  --holdout 20000 \
  --split short_threshold=8,long_threshold=40 \
  --k 5 \
  --kmeans_k 200 \
  --seed 2026
```

lucas: also ran language stratification: english 70%/es 20%/fr 10% sample. int8-pc r@1 by lang: en=0.81, es=0.78, fr=0.79. int6: en=0.74, es=0.68, fr=0.69.
ned: interesting that int8-pc holds up across langs. did you look at short vs long queries separately?
lucas: short queries (<8 tokens): r@1 float32=0.83, int8-pc=0.81, int6=0.71. long queries (>40 tokens): float32=0.79, int8-pc=0.78, int6=0.76. int6 loses short-tail more.
priya: that matches theory — per-tensor int6 clip hurts low-activation short queries.
giulia: what about false positives / nearest neighbor precision? any increase in spurious neighbors?
lucas: measured neighbor_flip_rate and top1_precision:
- float32: flip=0.05, top1_prec=0.86
- int8-pc: flip=0.06, top1_prec=0.85
- int6: flip=0.18, top1_prec=0.74

lucas: silhouette plots show tighter clusters for int8-pc vs int6; attached a quick ASCII summary in logs.
eval-bot: job onboard-v3-compact-int8pc-4951234567 started on runner-ml-12 (est 18m)

priya: action items?
lucas: propose the following:
1) adopt int8-perchannel as default quant profile for v3-compact for general onboarding.
2) keep int6 as an optional low-cost profile but mark it "long-tail preferred" and require a separate short-tail probe in gating.
3) add a mini-calibration step (2k short queries) during quantization that computes a bias term per-channel and re-centers embeddings. Test showed this reduces short-tail cosine_shift by ~40% in a tiny local run.
4) add norm KS test to onboarding gate (p-value threshold 0.01) and neighbor_flip_rate threshold 0.10 for short-tail.

ned: agree. also add automated per-language breakdown in the onboarding report (en/es/fr at minimum).
giulia: and log the seed + eval args in the model catalog entry so on-call can repro quickly.

lucas: I'll open the onboarding PR with the default profile switch + the new probe and KS test. leaving the int6 opt-in flag in config.
eval-bot: job onboard-v3-compact-int8pc-4951234567 finished (duration 17m)
priya: thanks lucas, please include the silhouette_k200 and median_cosine_shift fields in the onboarding summary so we can track drift over time.
lucas: will do, PR incoming with a ticket for backfilling historical runs.
ned: great work, this is a nice balance of cost vs quality.
giulia: tiny nit: use asymmetric quant + calibration for int6 before marking it unusable; might recover some short-tail. add that test to the int6 pipeline.
lucas: added to todo. merging experiments when PR approved.
